sources.gloss: He raises from every nation a witness, who is its prophet, testifying about how it responded to what he conveyed to it from God.

title.en: Justice, oaths, and refuge from Satan

essay.en:
The passage opens with a single verse of command and prohibition: God enjoins justice, kindness, and generosity towards relatives, and forbids indecency, wrongdoing, and aggression. Tabatabai reads the three commands as the foundation on which the whole structure of human society rests [1]. Reports preserved by the commentators add an occasion: Uthman ibn Maz'un embraced Islam the moment he heard this verse recited [2].

From conduct the passage turns to trust. Believers are told to fulfill the covenant of God once they pledge it, and not to break their oaths after binding them, having made God their guarantor. They must not be like the woman who unravels her spun yarn thread by thread after twisting it firm; commentators name her a foolish woman of Mecca called Rayta, whom God made a parable [6]. Oaths are not to be turned into instruments of deceit, trading a solemn word for advantage because one party outnumbers another. Several commentators tie these verses to the pledge given to the Prophet on accepting Islam [5].

A reminder follows that had God willed, He would have made all people one community; instead He leaves them to their choice and will question them for it. The passage then weighs the two rewards: what people hold runs out, but what is with God lasts, and the patient are paid by the best of their deeds. Whoever acts righteously and remains faithful, man or woman alike, is promised a good life, which the commentators variously read as contentment, lawful provision, or life in the Garden [8].

It closes with recitation and protection: when you recite the Quran, seek refuge in God from the outcast Satan, who holds no authority over those who believe and trust their Lord, only over those who befriend him and set up partners with God.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: الْعَدْلُ الْإِنْصَافُ، وَالْإِحْسَانُ التَّفَضُّلُ.

text.en: Justice is fairness, and kindness is bestowing favor beyond what is due.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: نعم ليس لله في عباده أمر إلا العدل والإِحسان فالدعاء من الله عام والهدى خاص مثل قوله: { ويهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Musa ibn Imran, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Ismail ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Yes. God has no command among His servants except justice and kindness. The call from God is general, but the guidance is specific, as He says: 'and He guides whomever He wishes to a straight path.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: العدل النبي والإحسان علي بن أبي طالب وذي القربى فاطمة عليهم الصلاة والسلام
narrations.chain: Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed al-Ahmasi, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Justice is the Prophet, kindness is Ali ibn Abi Talib, and generosity to relatives is Fatimah, peace be upon them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لما نزلت الولاية وكان من قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله بغدير خم سلموا على علي بإمرة المؤمنين عليه السلام فقالوا: أمن الله ورسوله؟ فقال لهم: نعم حقاً من الله ورسوله … وأنزل الله عز وجل { ولا تنقضوا الأيمان بعد توكيدها.. } الخ يعني: قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله من الله ورسوله
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raising it, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When the wilaya was revealed, the Messenger of God said at Ghadir Khumm, 'Greet Ali as Commander of the Faithful.' They asked, 'Is this from God and His Messenger?' He said, 'Yes, truly from God and His Messenger.' Then God revealed: do not break your oaths after confirming them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قال سيدنا الصادق (عليه السلام) في قوله: { فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَيَاةً طَيِّبَةً } قال: القنوع
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Jafar, from al-Sadiq

text.en: Concerning 'We shall revive him with a good life,' al-Sadiq said: it is contentment.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لعن الله أبا الخطاب والله ما قلت له هكذا ولكني قلت: إذا عرفت الحق فاعمل ما شئت من خير يقبل منك، إن الله عز وجل يقول: { من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة يرزقون فيها بغير حساب } ويقول تبارك وتعالى: { من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فلنحيينه حياة طيبة }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: God curse Abu al-Khattab. By God, I never said that to him. I said: when you know the truth, do whatever good you wish and it will be accepted from you. For God says: whoever acts righteously, male or female, being faithful, We shall revive him with a good life.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: تقول: أستعيذ بالله السميع العليم من الشيطان الرجيم … إن الرجيم أخبث الشياطين … لأنه يرجم
narrations.chain: from Sammaa, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Say: I seek refuge in God, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Satan the outcast. The outcast is the vilest of the satans. He is called the outcast because he is stoned.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ يُسَلَّطُ وَ اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ عَلَى بَدَنِهِ وَ لَا يُسَلَّطُ عَلَى دِينِهِ قَدْ سُلِّطَ عَلَى أَيُّوبَ (عليه السلام) فَشَوَّهَ خَلْقَهُ وَ لَمْ يُسَلَّطْ عَلَى دِينِهِ وَ قَدْ يُسَلَّطُ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَى أَبْدَانِهِمْ وَ لَا يُسَلَّطُ عَلَى دِينِهِمْ
narrations.chain: from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: O Abu Muhammad, by God, he is given power over the believer's body but not over his religion. He was given power over Ayyub and disfigured his body, yet not over his religion. So too he may afflict believers' bodies, never their religion.

perspectives.en: Sunni and Shia commentators share the plain sense of these verses but part on the oath and covenant. Sunni exegesis, following reports from the Companions, reads the confirmed oath as the general pledge given to the Prophet on accepting Islam, or as pre-Islamic tribal alliances that Islam told believers to honor [25]. Shia narrations read the same verses more narrowly: the covenant that must not be broken is the pledge to Ali as Commander of the Faithful, taken at Ghadir Khumm, when some asked whether the order came from God or only from His Messenger [10].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ابتدأ سبحانه بهذه الأحكام الثلاثة التي هي بالترتيب أهم ما يقوم به صلب المجتمع الإِنساني

sources.gloss: He began with these three commands, which in order are the most important things by which the backbone of human society stands.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فأتاني بهذه الآية { إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان } وقرأها عليَّ إلى آخرها فقرَّ الإسلام في قلبي

sources.gloss: He brought me this verse, 'Indeed Allah enjoins justice and kindness,' and recited it to me to the end, and Islam settled in my heart.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقيل: إِن الآية نزلت في الذين بايعوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الاسلام.

sources.gloss: It is said the verse was revealed about those who pledged allegiance to the Prophet upon Islam.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قيل: إِنها ريطة بنت عمرو بن كعب ابن سعيد بن تميم بن مرة، وكانت حمقاء، فضربه الله مثلاً

sources.gloss: It is said she was Rayta bint Amr ibn Kab, and she was foolish, so God made her a parable.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال ابن عباس: الحياة الطيبة هو الرزق الحلال. وقال الحسن: هي القناعة. وقال قتادة: حياة طيبة في الجنة.

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas said the good life is lawful provision; al-Hasan said it is contentment; Qatada said it is a good life in Paradise.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: ليس لله في عباده أمر إلا العدل والإِحسان

sources.gloss: God has no command among His servants except justice and kindness.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: لما نزلت الولاية وكان من قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله بغدير خم سلموا على علي بإمرة المؤمنين

sources.gloss: When the wilaya was revealed, the Messenger of God said at Ghadir Khumm: greet Ali as Commander of the Faithful.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قال سيدنا الصادق (عليه السلام) في قوله: { فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَيَاةً طَيِّبَةً } قال: القنوع

sources.gloss: Al-Sadiq said, concerning 'We shall revive him with a good life': it is contentment.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الرجيم أخبث الشياطين … لأنه يرجم

sources.gloss: The outcast is the vilest of the satans; he is called the outcast because he is stoned.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: العدل النبي والإحسان علي بن أبي طالب وذي القربى فاطمة عليهم الصلاة والسلام

sources.gloss: Justice is the Prophet, kindness is Ali ibn Abi Talib, and generosity to relatives is Fatimah, peace be upon them.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: أنزلت هذه الآية فـي بـيعة النبـيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، كان من أسلـم بـايع علـى الإسلام

sources.gloss: This verse was revealed about the pledge to the Prophet; whoever accepted Islam pledged upon Islam.

sources.author: al-sharif al-radi

excerpt.text: الْعَدْلُ الْإِنْصَافُ، وَالْإِحْسَانُ التَّفَضُّلُ

sources.gloss: Justice is fairness, and kindness is bestowing favor.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: إذا عرفت الحق فاعمل ما شئت من خير يقبل منك

sources.gloss: When you know the truth, do whatever good you wish and it will be accepted from you.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: يُسَلَّطُ وَ اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ عَلَى بَدَنِهِ وَ لَا يُسَلَّطُ عَلَى دِينِهِ

sources.gloss: By God, he is given power over the believer's body but not over his religion.

essay.en: The passage answers three charges the Meccans flung at the Prophet. First, when a revealed ruling replaces an earlier one - 'When We change a sign for another in its stead' - they call him a fabricator. The commentators read this as abrogation: God alone knows the changing interests a ruling serves, so He replaces one with another as the good of His servants requires [1][3][5]. Tabatabai holds the objectors are the idolaters, though it was the Jews who were most rigid in denying that any ruling could be abrogated [1]. The reply comes at once: 'the Holy Spirit has brought it down' - Gabriel, from your Lord in truth, to steady the believers and guide the Muslims. Tabatabai distinguishes the two gifts: firmness belongs to faith, the heart's share, while guidance and good news belong to islam, the outward following of the limbs [1]. The second charge is that a man teaches him. The Quran answers that the tongue of the one they point to is foreign, 'while this is a clear Arabic language.' Tabatabai argues the reply does not stop at language but runs through the next verses, for one whom God has guided does not invent lies against Him [1]. So the charge is turned back: 'Only those fabricate lies who do not believe in the signs of Allah' [1][7]. The passage then turns to those who disbelieve after faith, and excepts the one compelled while 'his heart is at rest in it' - the verse of Ammar ibn Yasir, tortured until he yielded with his tongue [2][4]. Those who instead 'open up their breasts to unfaith,' who preferred this world and whose hearts God has sealed, are the losers [2][9]. It closes with mercy: for those who migrated after persecution, waged jihad and stood firm, their Lord is forgiving and merciful [2][4].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: هو جبرئيل (عليه السلام)، و القدس: الطاهر { لِيُثَبِّتَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ } هم آل محمد (عليهم السلام) { وَهُدًى وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ }
narrations.chain: Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar al-Baqir

text.en: The Holy Spirit is Gabriel, and al-Quds means the pure. 'To fortify those who have faith' - they are the family of Muhammad - 'and as guidance and good news for the Muslims.'

note.en: Commentary names the foreigner as Abu Fukayha, a freedman from the People of the Book whose speech was non-Arabic; Quraysh claimed he taught the Prophet, while the Quran itself is clear Arabic [13].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: أنه ذكر رجلا كذابا ثم قال: قال الله: { إِنَّمَا يَفْتَرِي ٱلْكَذِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Abbas ibn Hilal, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida

text.en: He mentioned a certain liar, then said: God says, 'Only those fabricate lies who do not believe in the signs of Allah.'

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
narrations.arabic: فهو عمار بن ياسر أخذته قريش بمكة فعذبوه بالنار حتى أعطاهم بلسانه ما أرادوا وقلبه مطمئن بالإِيمان وأما قوله { ولكن من شرح بالكفر صدراً } فهو عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح بن الحارث من بني لوي.

text.en: This is Ammar ibn Yasir: Quraysh seized him at Mecca and tortured him with fire until he gave them what they wanted with his tongue, while his heart was at rest with faith. 'But whoever opens up his breast to unfaith' is Abdullah ibn Sad ibn Abi Sarh.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ما منع ميثم التمار (رحمه الله) من التقية؟ فو الله، لقد علم أن هذه الآية نزلت في عمار و أصحابه: { إِلاَّ مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِٱلإِيمَانِ }
narrations.chain: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: What kept Maytham al-Tammar - may God have mercy on him - from taqiyya? By God, he knew that this verse came down about Ammar and his companions: 'except someone who is compelled while his heart is at rest in faith.'

narrations.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله): رفعت عن أمتي أربع خصال: ما أخطأوا، و ما نسوا، و ما اكرهوا عليه، و ما لم يطيقوا، و ذلك في كتاب الله: { إِلاَّ مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِٱلإِيمَانِ }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Amr ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah, from the Messenger of Allah

text.en: My community is relieved of four things: what they do in error, what they forget, what they are compelled to do, and what they cannot bear - and that is in God's Book: 'except someone who is compelled while his heart is at rest in faith.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) كان يدعو أصحابه، فمن أراد به خيرا سمع و عرف ما يدعوه إليه، و من أراد به شرا طبع عليه قلبه فلا يسمع و لا يعقل، و هو قوله: { أُولَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ طَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ وَسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَارِهِمْ وَأُولَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْغَافِلُونَ }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The Messenger of Allah would summon his companions. Whomever God wished good for heard and grasped what he was called to; whomever God wished ill for, his heart was sealed so he neither heard nor understood. That is His saying, 'They are the ones Allah has set a seal on their hearts.'

perspectives.en: Shia and Sunni tafsir agree that 16:106 was revealed about Ammar ibn Yasir, compelled under torture to utter unbelief while his heart held firm, and that God excused him. They differ in emphasis. The Shia narrations make the verse the charter of taqiyya: 'taqiyya is the shield of the believer, and there is no faith for one who has no taqiyya,' and the Imams invoke it so a believer need not choose death over dissimulation [20]. Sunni commentators allow the same concession but hold that standing firm to the point of death is the more meritorious course [34][40].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: إشارة إلى النسخ وحكمته، وجواب عما اتهموه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم به من الافتراء على الله

sources.gloss: A reference to abrogation and its wisdom, and an answer to their accusing him of fabrication against God.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: في الآيات وعيد على الكفر بعد الإِيمان وهو الارتداد ووعد جميل للمهاجرين من بعد ما فتنوا المجاهدين الصابرين في الله، وفيها تعرّض لحكم التقيّة

sources.gloss: In these verses is a threat against unbelief after faith - which is apostasy - and a beautiful promise for those who migrated after being persecuted, who strove and were patient; and they touch on the ruling of taqiyya.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: معناه وإذا نسخنا آية مكانها آية أخرى … والله أعلم بمصالح ما ينزل كل وقت ما توجبه المصلحة

sources.gloss: It means: when We abrogate a verse and put another in its place, and God knows best the interests of what He sends down at each moment, as the benefit requires.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { إلا من أكره } فتكلم بكلمة الكفر على وجه التقية مكرها { وقلبه مطمئن } أي ساكن { بالإِيمان } ثابت عليه فلا حرج عليه في ذلك

sources.gloss: 'Except one compelled' - he uttered the word of unbelief by way of taqiyya, under compulsion, while his heart was at rest, settled and firm upon faith; so there is no blame on him in that.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: بأن رفعنا آية ونسخناها، وأتينا بأخرى بدلها … يعني القرآن نزله جبريل (ع)

sources.gloss: That We lift a verse and abrogate it, bringing another in its place; 'the Holy Spirit brought it down' means Gabriel brought down the Quran.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: الذي يتخرص الكذب، ويفتري على الله، هو الذي لا يؤمن بآيات الله

sources.gloss: The one who invents lies and fabricates against God is the one who does not believe in God's signs.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: { لا جرم أنهم } معناه حقَّ لهم { أنهم في الآخرة هم الخاسرون } الذين خسروا صفقتهم لفوات الثواب وحصول العقاب

sources.gloss: 'Undoubtedly they' means it is confirmed for them 'that in the Hereafter they are the losers' - who lost their bargain, missing the reward and incurring the punishment.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وهو لسان أبي فكيهة مولى ابن الحضرمي كان أعجمي اللسان وكان قد اتبع نبي الله وآمن به وكان من أهل الكتاب فقالت قريش هذا والله يعلم محمداً بلسانه

sources.gloss: It is the tongue of Abu Fukayha, a freedman of Ibn al-Hadrami, who was non-Arabic in speech, had followed God's Prophet and believed in him, and was from the People of the Book; Quraysh said, 'By God, this man teaches Muhammad in his own tongue.'

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فهو عمار بن ياسر أخذته قريش بمكة فعذبوه بالنار حتى أعطاهم بلسانه ما أرادوا وقلبه مطمئن بالإِيمان

sources.gloss: It is Ammar ibn Yasir; Quraysh seized him at Mecca and tortured him with fire until he gave them what they wanted with his tongue, while his heart was at rest with faith.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: { لِيُثَبِّتَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ } هم آل محمد

sources.gloss: 'To fortify those who have faith' - they are the family of Muhammad.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أنه ذكر رجلا كذابا ثم قال: قال الله: { إِنَّمَا يَفْتَرِي ٱلْكَذِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ }

sources.gloss: He mentioned a certain liar, then said: God says, 'Only those fabricate lies who do not believe.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن التقية ترس المؤمن، و لا إيمان لمن لا تقية له

sources.gloss: Taqiyya is the shield of the believer, and there is no faith for one who has no taqiyya.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: والأفضل والأولى أن يثبت المسلم على دينه ولو أفضى إلى قتله

sources.gloss: The more virtuous and preferable is that the Muslim stand firm on his religion, even if it leads to his being killed.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: أجمع العلماء على أن من أكره على الكفر فاختار القتل أنه أعظم أجراً عند الله

sources.gloss: The scholars agree that whoever is compelled to unbelief and chooses death has a greater reward with God.

essay.en:
The Day arrives when every soul comes pleading for itself. al-Mizan sees each soul so consumed with its own defense that it forgets all else, since it is then repaid the very deed it did, without addition or reduction, in perfect justice [1]. To drive the warning home, God sets a parable: a town that was secure, at peace, and supplied abundantly from every side grew ungrateful for His blessings and rejected the messenger raised from among it, so it was made to taste hunger and fear. al-Mizan reads this as a general parable about ingratitude, while Majma al-Bayan records the view that the town is Mecca [2][3].

From the parable follows a directive: eat of the lawful and good that God has provided, and give thanks. al-Mizan holds that this command grants permission rather than obligation, and that it addresses the believers who worship God alone [2]. God then limits the forbidden foods to four - carrion, blood, swine, and what is offered to other than Him - with mercy for anyone driven to them by necessity.

Next the passage forbids the tongue its false verdicts of 'this is lawful, this is unlawful.' al-Mizan reads this as a ban on inventing rulings God never sent down, a lie against Him even when it is not openly ascribed to Him [2]. Such invention buys only a trifling enjoyment and a painful punishment.

Turning to the Jews, God recalls that what He forbade them earlier was a penalty for wronging themselves, not a wrong done to them [2]. The passage then rests on mercy: for those who did evil in ignorance - which al-Tibyan takes as either genuine ignorance or the heedlessness of one whose desire overpowers his reason [10], and which al-Mizan restricts to the latter, since utter unawareness would leave no sin to repent of [2] - then repented and set themselves right, the Lord is forgiving and merciful.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: و إن قوما أفرغت عليهم النعمة - و هم أهل الثرثار - فعمدوا إلى مخ الحنطة فجعلوه خبزا هجاء، و جعلوا ينجون به صبيانهم حتى اجتمع من ذلك جبل عظيم … فأسف الله عز و جل، فأضعف لهم الثرثار، و حبس عنهم قطر السماء و نبات الأرض … فاحتاجوا إلى ذلك الجبل، و إنه كان يقسم بينهم بالميزان
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: A people had abundance poured over them, the people of Thrthar. They took the core of the wheat, baked it into loaves, and cleaned their children with it until a great mound piled up. So God was angered: he reduced their river and withheld rain and growth, until they needed that mound and rationed it out by the scale.

note.en: al-Tibyan, following Mujahid and the Shia scholars, glosses the 'rebellious' person excluded from this permission as one who has risen against a just imam [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إذا قال للحلال هذا حرام وللحرام هذا حلال ودان بذلك فعندما يكون خارجاً من الإيمان والإسلام إلى الكفر، وكان بمنزلة رجل دخل الحرم ثم دخل الكعبة فأحدث في الكعبة حدثاً فأخرج عن الكعبة وعن الحرم فضربت عنقه وصار إلى النار

text.en: When someone calls the lawful unlawful and the unlawful lawful and takes that as his religion, at that point he passes out of faith and Islam into unbelief. He is like a man who entered the sanctuary, then the Ka'ba, and defiled it, so he is expelled from both, his neck is struck, and he goes to the Fire.

perspectives.en: The commentators divide over which town verse 112 pictures. al-Tabari reports the majority Sunni view, from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatada, that it is Mecca, struck with years of hunger through the Prophet's supplication while its people feared his raiding parties [19]. al-Mizan prefers to read it as a general parable of any community that God favors and that then turns ungrateful, though it grants that Mecca fits [2]. The Shia narrations take a third path, tying the town to an earlier people, the people of Thrthar, ruined for wasting the bounty poured on them [13].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ومجادلة النفس عن نفسها دفاعها عن نفسها وقد نسيت كل شيء وراء نفسها

sources.gloss: A soul's pleading for itself is its defense of itself, having forgotten everything beyond itself.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: سياق الآيات إنما يلائم كونه مثلاً عاماً

sources.gloss: The flow of the verses fits its being a general parable.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقيل إن هذه القرية هي مكة عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة عذبهم الله بالجوع سبع سنين

sources.gloss: It is said this town is Mecca - from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatada - whom God punished with hunger for seven years.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وان قول مجاهد وما ذهب اليه أصحابنا هو من خرج على امام عادل

sources.gloss: The view of Mujahid and of our companions is that it is one who has risen against a just imam.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فقد يكون ذلك للجاهل بالشيء وقد يكون للغافل الذي يعمل عمل الجاهل بتغليب هواه على عقله

sources.gloss: It may be one ignorant of the thing, or the heedless person who acts like the ignorant by letting his desire overpower his reason.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و إن قوما أفرغت عليهم النعمة - و هم أهل الثرثار - فعمدوا إلى مخ الحنطة فجعلوه خبزا هجاء، و جعلوا ينجون به صبيانهم حتى اجتمع من ذلك جبل عظيم

sources.gloss: A people had abundance poured over them, the people of Thrthar; they took the core of the wheat, baked it into loaves, and cleaned their children with it until a great mound gathered.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: فاذا قال للحلال هذا حرام وللحرام هذا حلال ودان بذلك فعندما يكون خارجاً من الايمان والاسلام إلى الكفر

sources.gloss: So when he calls the lawful unlawful and the unlawful lawful and takes that as religion, at that point he passes out of faith and Islam into unbelief.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: ومثل الله مثلاً لـمكّة التـي سكانها أهل الشرك بـالله هي القرية التـي كانت آمنة مطمئنة

sources.gloss: God set a parable for Mecca, whose inhabitants were people of idolatry; it is the town that was secure and at peace.

essay.en:
These verses close the surah. After the long passage on lawful and forbidden foods and on abrogation, the surah turns to Abraham to show that what was revealed to the Prophet is nothing other than Abraham's own creed: a balanced religion, in keeping with human nature, that permits good things and forbids foul ones [1]. Abraham is praised as 'a nation,' which the commentators read as a model and teacher of good in whom a whole community stood [2], obedient to God, a Hanif inclining to the balanced middle between extremes [1], grateful, chosen, and guided to a straight path. God gave him good in this world and placed him among the righteous.

The Prophet is then told to follow the creed of Abraham. Commentators note that the superior is here directed to one lesser only because Abraham was first to reach the truth, and there is no disparagement in following one who preceded [2]. A verse on the Sabbath follows: it was imposed as a burden on those who differed over it. The surah sets their quarrel beside its warning against differing over the truth [4], and God will judge their differences on the Day of Resurrection.

The surah's method of calling is then laid out: wisdom, good exhortation, and disputation in the manner that is best. Al-Mizan maps these three to demonstration, exhortation, and dialectic, noting that disputation is licensed only in its finest form [1], while Majma reads the wisdom as the Quran itself [3]. The close counsels measured retaliation and prefers patience; the reports place these final verses after Uhud [3]. The Prophet is told to be steadfast, and that his steadfastness is only through God [1]. The surah ends on a promise: God is with the Godwary and the virtuous, each quality on its own drawing His help [1].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الامة واحد فصاعدا، كما قال الله عز و جل: { إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ كَانَ أُمَّةً قَانِتاً لِلَّهِ } يقول: مطيعا لله عز و جل
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The word 'nation' means one person or more, as God said, 'Indeed Abraham was a nation obedient to Allah' - that is, obedient to Allah.

narrations.speaker: the Righteous Servant
narrations.arabic: لقد كانت الدنيا، و ما كان فيها إلا واحد يعبد الله، و لو كان معه غيره إذن لأضافه إليه حيث يقول: { إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ كَانَ أُمَّةً قَانِتاً لِلَّهِ حَنِيفاً وَلَمْ يَكُ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ } فصبر بذلك ما شاء الله، ثم إن الله تبارك و تعالى آنسه بإسماعيل و إسحاق فصاروا ثلاثة
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Samaa ibn Mihran, from the Righteous Servant

text.en: There was a time when the whole world held only one man who worshipped Allah; had another been with him, Allah would have joined him to him. So God said, 'Indeed Abraham was a nation.' He endured as God willed, then God comforted him with Ismail and Ishaq, so they became three.

note.en: Tafsir al-Qummi glosses the creed of Abraham as the ten practices of the Hanifiyya, five of the body and five of the head, which have not been abrogated to the Day of Resurrection [7].
Tafsir al-Qummi relates that Moses commanded his people to devote to God one day in every seven, and it was over this day that they later differed [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لم ينه عنه مطلقا و لكنه نهى عن الجدال بغير التي هي أحسن … فالجدال بالتي هي أحسن قد قرنه العلماء بالدين، و الجدال بغير التي هي أحسن محرم، حرمه الله تعالى على شيعتنا
narrations.chain: al-Imam al-Askari, that al-Sadiq said

text.en: He did not forbid disputation absolutely; He forbade only disputation in other than the best manner. Disputation in the best manner the scholars of religion have joined to the faith, while disputation in a worse manner God has forbidden to our Shia.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: في قوله تعالى: { ٱدْعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَٱلْمَوْعِظَةِ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ وَجَٰدِلْهُم بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ } … قال: بالقرآن
narrations.chain: al-Kulayni, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Abu Amr al-Zubayri, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Concerning His words, 'Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good advice, and dispute with them in a manner that is best' - he said: by means of the Quran.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لما رأى رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) ما صنع بحمزة بن عبد المطلب، قال: اللهم لك الحمد، و إليك المشتكى، و أنت المستعان على ما أرى. ثم قال: لئن ظفرت لأمثلن و لأمثلن. قال: فأنزل الله: { وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُواْ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ وَلَئِن صَبَرْتُمْ لَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لِّلصَّابِرينَ } فقال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله): أصبر، أصبر
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Husayn ibn Hamza, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When the Messenger of Allah saw what was done to Hamza, he said, 'O Allah, to You be praise, to You the complaint, and You are the one whose help is sought.' Then he said, 'If I win, I will mutilate.' So Allah sent down the verse, and the Messenger said, 'I will be patient, I will be patient.'

narrations.speaker: the Imam
narrations.arabic: كلف الله جميع الخلق ما لا يطيقونه، إن لم يعنهم عليه، فإن أعانهم عليه أطاقوه، قال الله جل و عز لنبيه (صلى الله عليه و آله): { وَٱصْبِرْ وَمَا صَبْرُكَ إِلاَّ بِٱللَّهِ }

text.en: Allah has charged all creation with what they cannot bear, if He does not help them; but if He helps them, they can bear it. Allah said to His Prophet, 'So be steadfast, and you cannot be steadfast except with Allah.'

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: يَا هَمَّامُ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ وَأَحْسِنْ فَ ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مُحْسِنُونَ﴾

text.en: O Hammam, fear Allah and do good, for 'Indeed Allah is with those who are Godwary and those who are virtuous.'

perspectives.en: Verse 123 tells the Prophet to follow the creed of Abraham, and the two traditions read the scope of that following differently. Sunni commentators such as al-Qurtubi hold that the sound view is following him in the creedal foundations of the religion, in tawhid and the disavowal of idols, rather than in its branches [25]. Shia reports narrow the creed of Abraham to the household of the Prophet: al-Safi relates from al-Husayn that no one is upon the creed of Abraham except the Imams and their Shia, the rest of the people being free of it [15].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وهي ملة معتدلة جارية على الفطرة تحلل الطيبات وتحرّم الخبائث

sources.gloss: This creed [of Abraham, revealed to the Prophet] is a balanced one, in keeping with human nature, permitting good things and forbidding foul ones.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فقيل قدوة ومعلماً للخير

sources.gloss: It is said [that 'a nation' means] a model and a teacher of good.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { بالحكمة } أي بالقرآن … وقالوا إن المشركين لما مثلوا بقتلى أحد وبحمزة بن عبد المطلب

sources.gloss: 'With wisdom' means with the Quran … and they said the polytheists mutilated the slain of Uhud and Hamza b. Abd al-Muttalib [when the verse came down].

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لما أمر باتباع الحق، حذّر من الاختلاف فيه، بما ذكره من حال المختلفين في السبت

sources.gloss: Having commanded the following of truth, He warned against differing over it, through what He mentioned of the state of those who differed over the Sabbath.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وهي الحنفية العشر التي جاء بها إبراهيم عليه السلام خمسة في البدن وخمسة في الرأس … فهذه لم تنسخ إلى يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: These are the ten practices of the Hanifiyya that Abraham brought, five in the body and five in the head … these have not been abrogated until the Day of Resurrection.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أن موسى أمر قومه أن يتفرغوا إلى الله في كل سبعة أيام يوماً يجعله الله عليهم وهم الذين اختلفوا فيه

sources.gloss: Moses commanded his people to devote to God one day in every seven, a day God laid upon them, and they are the ones who differed about it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الامة واحد فصاعدا، كما قال الله عز و جل: { إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ كَانَ أُمَّةً قَانِتاً لِلَّهِ } يقول: مطيعا لله عز و جل

sources.gloss: 'Nation' means one person or more, as God said, 'Indeed Abraham was a nation obedient to Allah' - that is, obedient to Allah.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لم ينه عنه مطلقا و لكنه نهى عن الجدال بغير التي هي أحسن

sources.gloss: He did not forbid it absolutely; He forbade only disputation in other than the best manner.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فأنزل الله: { وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُواْ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ وَلَئِن صَبَرْتُمْ لَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لِّلصَّابِرينَ } فقال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله): أصبر، أصبر

sources.gloss: So Allah sent down, 'Should you retaliate, retaliate with the like of what you have been made to suffer, but if you are patient that is surely better,' and the Messenger of Allah said, 'I will be patient, I will be patient.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: كلف الله جميع الخلق ما لا يطيقونه، إن لم يعنهم عليه، فإن أعانهم عليه أطاقوه

sources.gloss: Allah has charged all creation with what they cannot bear if He does not help them; but if He helps them, they can bear it.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ما احد على ملّة إبراهيم إلاّ نحن وشيعتنا وساير الناس منها براء

sources.gloss: No one is upon the creed of Abraham except us and our Shia; the rest of the people are free of it.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: والصحيح الاتباع في عقائد الشرع دون الفروع

sources.gloss: The sound view is following [Abraham] in the creedal foundations of the law, not in its branches.

sources.author: al-sharif al-radi

excerpt.text: يَا هَمَّامُ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ وَأَحْسِنْ فَ ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مُحْسِنُونَ﴾

sources.gloss: O Hammam, fear Allah and do good, for 'Indeed Allah is with those who are Godwary and those who are virtuous.'
